deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.15): U = U_{0,3} = P^1(C) - {0,1,inf} with the round metric, in which 0, 1, inf are equally spaced on a great circle. P and P̄ = e^{±i pi/3} are the poles fixed by the order-3 rotation rho(z) = 1/(1-z). The three transpositions sigma_0(z) = z/(z-1), sigma_1(z) = 1/z and sigma_inf(z) = 1-z are half-turns about the axes (0,2), (1,-1) and (inf,1/2). Complex conjugation tau is a reflection. Gamma = S_3 x Z/2 acts on U, and E = E_{0,3} is the extension of Gamma by pi = pi_1(U,P).

This page makes E explicit as the 'groupe fondamental mixte' (equivariant / orbifold fundamental group of the quotient stack [U/Gamma] at P). Following Malgoire, an element is a pair (gamma, l): gamma in Gamma, and l a homotopy class of paths from P to gamma^{-1}(P). The product is (gamma,l)(gamma',l') = (gamma gamma', gamma'^{-1}(l) ∘ l').
- Typing checks: l' runs from P to gamma'^{-1}P, and gamma'^{-1}(l) runs from gamma'^{-1}P to (gamma gamma')^{-1}P.
- Paths compose 'like functions'. This is the convention making the fundamental groupoid act on the left on fibres of an étale cover, with l: x -> y giving l_*: U'_x -> U'_y.

He then chooses explicit lifts sigma_i-dot = (sigma_i, path from P to P̄ = sigma_i P). The path is the half great circle from P to P̄ in the mirror plane of the reflection tau sigma_i = sigma_i tau. That plane contains P, P̄ and a_i, and the reflection swaps the other two a_j, a_k. Since a_i is a puncture, the admissible half-circle is the one through the antipode of a_i (2, -1, 1/2); the marginal '(pour 1 : -1)' suggests this.

l_0, l_1, l_inf are the positive loops from P around 0, 1, inf along great-circle segments. With the functional convention the surface relation reads (1) l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1, not l_0 l_1 l_inf = 1. The next page continues with sigma_i-dot^2 = 1, sigma_0-dot sigma_1-dot = rho-dot l_0, etc., and an attempted presentation of E that he marks 'C'est faux'.

Purpose: an explicit, symmetric presentation of the extension of S_3 x Z/2 by pi_{0,3}. This is the basic 'level 0, dimension 1' building block of the Teichmüller tower / Galois action program (Longue Marche, Esquisse), with complex conjugation included in the symmetry group. Classically, E is the extended modular group PGL_2(Z): the S_3 quotient of the lambda-line is the j-line, and P corresponds to j = 0, the order-3 orbifold point. The page does not say this explicitly.
errors: The text says the path from P to P̄ 'passes through a_i'. a_i is a puncture, so the admissible half great circle in the mirror plane of tau sigma_i must be the one through the antipode of a_i (2, -1 or 1/2); the marginal '(pour 1 : -1)' indicates this. Either a slip or a transcription issue.
No error in the product law or in relation (1) under the stated convention. The presentation attempted on the following page is flagged by Grothendieck himself as wrong ('C'est faux').

ideas.what: Equivariant ('mixed') fundamental group of a Gamma-space, as pairs (gamma, path from P to gamma^{-1}P) with a twisted composition law
ideas.modern_name: orbifold / stacky fundamental group of [U/Gamma]; fundamental group of the action groupoid; equivariant fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Armstrong, Brown's groupoid methods, Haefliger/Thurston orbifolds); in the Grothendieck circle attributed here to J. Malgoire
ideas.where_published: the extension-of-Gamma-by-pi viewpoint is in SGA1 Exp. XIII / Esquisse and Longue Marche; the explicit Malgoire pair formalism is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Symmetric base point P = e^{i pi/3} (fixed point of the 3-cycle), with lifts of the transpositions defined by half great circles in the mirror planes of tau sigma_i
ideas.modern_name: symmetric (non-tangential) base point for the S_3 x Z/2-action on M_{0,4}; real structures / complex conjugation in the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and Drinfeld use tangential base points; S_3-symmetric choices appear in Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps and related GT literature
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (1981) discusses pi_{0,4} with its symmetries; exact construction not known in print

ideas.what: Product relation l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1 under the 'composition as functions' convention
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche (generators of pi_{0,3})

missed.claim: An explicit model of the extension of S_3 x Z/2 by pi_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}), including complex conjugation, at a symmetric base point with geometrically chosen order-2 lifts. It is a hands-on precursor of the order-2 and order-3 relations of GT-hat. The group is classically PGL_2(Z). Nothing seems mathematically new; it is mainly a historical document of Grothendieck's working conventions and of Malgoire's formalism.
missed.quote: Le groupe fondamental mixte est défini à la Malgoire, les classes (γ,λ) d'un γ∈Γ et d'une classe de chemins ℓ de P dans γ^{-1}(P)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the early (1981) role of complex conjugation and S_3-symmetric base points in Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower program, and the attribution of the equivariant-groupoid formalism to Malgoire.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard construction of an orbifold fundamental group with explicit generators and conventions; historically interesting as part of the 1981 Galois–Teichmüller work, but contains no result unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'Le g[?]pe fondamental mixte' = 'Le groupe fondamental mixte'.
'${}^{\ell}/$de P dans γ^{-1}(P)' should read 'ℓ de P dans γ^{-1}(P)' (λ and ℓ denote the same path class).
'sur les fibres ∫_{U'} d'un rev. étale' is likely 'sur les fibres U'_x d'un revêtement étale U''.
'{+de δ_i[?]+}' likely 'de σ_i' or 'de P à P̄'.
'{+aux. au pts fixes+}' likely 'ens. des pts fixes' (the fixed set of the reflection τσ_i).
'(pour λ(-1))' likely '(pour i=1 : −1)', meaning the half-circle passes through the antipode −1 rather than through a_i.
'en allant vers [-∞, 4,-] ∞' likely 'en allant vers 0, 1, ∞ suivant des segments de grands cercles'.
